## Why

On npm, `pm-context` links **Homepage** to `https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context#readme`, the same place as the Repository link beside it. The package has its page in the pm cli package catalog: https://pm-cli.unbrained.dev/packages/pm-context. Pointing npm there gives people a useful place to land and lets search engines tie the package to its website. The author field (`"@unbraind"`) has no link to the person behind the work.

## What to change

In `package.json`:

```json
"homepage": "https://pm-cli.unbrained.dev/packages/pm-context",
"author": { "name": "unbrained", "url": "https://unbrained.dev/about" },
```

- Currently: `"homepage": "https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context#readme"`, `"author": "@unbraind"`.
- Keep `repository` and `bugs` as they are.
- Set the repository's GitHub website (About → Website) to the same address (currently empty): `gh repo edit unbraind/pm-context --homepage https://pm-cli.unbrained.dev/packages/pm-context`.
- npm takes the new fields with the next published version.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `npm view pm-context homepage` prints `https://pm-cli.unbrained.dev/packages/pm-context` after the next release.
- [ ] `npm view pm-context author` includes the url `https://unbrained.dev/about`.
- [ ] The GitHub repository's website is `https://pm-cli.unbrained.dev/packages/pm-context`.

## Context

Checked 2026-10-25 with `npm view` and the GitHub API. The same change has been filed in every published unbrained package's repository (pm-cli as unbraind/pm-cli#1594, its extensions, pm-web and the agent-ready clis), so they all link the same way: the product page as homepage, https://unbrained.dev/about as the author.
